chapters.fx: What to watch: CPI Wednesday 7:30am CT — consensus 3.6-3.7% y/y, core m/m 0.2%, core y/y 2.5%; the audition for the December hike. Fed voices today: Waller, Barkin, Collins; Warsh Thursday 10:30pm CT — then the blackout starts Saturday Oct 17. US data today is light: existing home sales 9am CT, NFIB ~11am CT, weekly ADP ~1:15pm CT. Big bank earnings pre-open (JPM, Goldman, Wells, Citi) set the earnings-season tone.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the dollar gave back a slice of Monday's 1.5-year high, with DXY sliding 0.2% to ~102.39-102.44 in the Asian session. Two of Monday's three fuels reversed — crude's war premium leaked (Brent -1.4% to ~$105 on Russian diesel-supply prospects and an OFAC general license for Russian diesel through April 2027) and the US 10-year fell 5bp to 5.19% as bonds reopened after the holiday. MUFG's read: "signs that positive global economic surprises are coming off the boil, while US bond yields are stabilising." Thread: the hawkish hold is in week five; Monday the war bid and the rate bid stacked into the top. What it means: the dollar's two engines are diverging — the rate bid is intact (FedWatch still ~19% for October, ~86% for December; Hammack's "rates need to move higher" stands) but the war bid is leaking. The top stalls until one of them re-accelerates.

What it means: confirms the prior thesis — sterling remains the best of the European losers, floored by the BoE's hawkish hold while the euro deals with its own fiscal drama.

chapters.meaning: What changed: the franc drifted with the dollar's tide, not with fear — USD/CHF eased 0.2% to ~0.8330, still pinned near the 52-week high of 0.8383. Overnight brought real escalation (Houthis claim Saudi airstrikes on Kamaran island, Qanawis and Jawf; ~60% of Riyadh airport's Monday flights cancelled), yet the franc saw no haven bid. Thread: Monday the dollar won the haven race outright (USD/CHF's +0.54% was the day's biggest dollar move); overnight the race didn't even start. What it means: fear is expressing through crude, not currencies — and Iran's offer to mediate Saudi-Houthi talks (~12:30am CT) gave the market a de-escalation headline to hold. EUR/CHF ~0.9308 shows the French stress still transmitting only lightly.

scenarios.base: The franc drifts with the dollar's tide; fear headlines keep failing to bid it.
scenarios.bear: De-escalation confirmed — the fear premium clears and USD/CHF tests the 52-week high.
scenarios.bull: A verified supply shock — the haven bid finally finds the franc and USD/CHF drops.

chapters.fx: What to watch: China CPI tonight 8:30pm CT (the demand read for the Aussie); Australia jobs Thursday (20K, unemployment 4.6%); RBA Nov 2-3 decision; Australia CPI Oct 28. Contrarian read: AUD shorts at the ~2nd percentile with record gross shorts — the most crowded short on the board after EUR/GBP; squeeze potential if the data turns.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the RBA minutes landed hawkish and the currency shrugged. The Sep 29 hike to 4.60% was unanimous; the board kept "continue to do what is needed... including increasing the cash rate target further if required"; upside inflation risks flagged in August are materializing — Middle East tensions pushing oil above forecasts, AI-demand cost pressures, domestic pass-throughs; delaying risked entrenching inflation, and holding risked AUD weakness as peers keep tightening. AUD/USD stayed ~0.6960-0.6962, below $0.70, near multi-month lows. Thread: Westpac expects one more hike by year-end; ANZ/UBS see a final 25bp to 4.85% while CBA/NAB see a hold; NAB business confidence printed -13, the 7th straight negative. What it means: confirms the best-in-G10 policy case — but the policy tailwind is losing to the sentiment headwind; the market is waiting for November 3, not re-reading September.

chapters.fx: What to watch: the OPEC monthly oil report today; whether the Iran mediation offer goes anywhere; physical diesel cargoes (the deal's real test, not the press release); the EIA weekly. Spread toward $15 = Hormuz risk back in force; toward $5 = premium truly unwinding. For FX: crude's pullback removes the tailwind for CAD and eases the tax on JPY/EUR.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Monday's $106.65 settle (highest since Sept 15) gave back ~1.4% overnight to ~$105-106 as two counter-forces met. The leak: Russia's 300k+ tonne diesel deal plus a temporary OFAC general license authorizing Russian diesel transactions through April 6, 2027 eased diesel-supply fears. The floor: the Houthis claim Saudi airstrikes overnight on Kamaran island, Qanawis and Jawf; ~60% of Riyadh airport's Monday flights were cancelled; Asian refiners bought 12M barrels of November Saudi crude in the spot market — some at a $20/barrel premium to official prices. Iran offered to mediate Saudi-Houthi talks (~12:30am CT) — de-escalation signal or theater, the market is watching. Thread: Monday the US session bought the war back (+$6.45 over three sessions); overnight the market sold part of the fade back. What it means: the premium is negotiable day to day now — the market prices a process, with escalation and de-escalation in the same session. The Brent-WTI spread at ~$12.5-13 stays wide: the premium is still shipping and geopolitics, not demand.

scenarios.base: Brent holds $103-108; the market needs a verified supply shock or a verified ceasefire to leave this range.
scenarios.bear: Ceasefire confirmation or fast restarts — Brent under $100, spread collapses toward $5.
scenarios.bull: Verified Hormuz disruption or Trump joining the Saudi campaign — Brent toward $110+, spread past $15.

chapters.meaning: What changed: gold recovered the ground it lost Monday — spot ran ~$4,195-4,198 (+0.6%) in Asia versus the $4,166 Comex settle, as the dollar's stall let the haven leg win the tug against 5.19% 10-year yields. The PBOC bought 740,000 oz in September — its 23rd straight month and largest since November 2024 — the structural bid under the trade. Thread: Monday's two-engine read had the dollar leg as the heavier engine; overnight the dollar leg weakened and gold responded exactly as the model says. What it means for FX: confirms the two-engine read — gold is the anti-dollar tell; it firms when the dollar softens and real yields stop rising. A soft CPI Wednesday would arm both engines at once.
